basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens '| Vers. 21. Trans turrim gregis. Gregis turrim dicit, id est gregis. Tradunt Judaei hic'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 21. Trans turrim gregis. Gregis turrim dicit, id est gregis. Tradunt Judaei hic postea templum Dei factum, unde turris gregis, id est multitudinis, congregationis, vel coetus appellatur. Beatus Hieronymus turrim gregis dicit turrim pastorum, quae est ultra Bethlehem, ubi pastores sancti angelico affatu natum Dominum cognoverunt, ubi etiam ipsorum trium pastorum corpora requiescunt. De hac turri per prophetam praedictum fuerat: Et tu turris gregis nebulosa, ad te veniet potestas prima filiae Sion (Mich. IV, 8).
